title: On the ν-zeros of the modified Bessel function K_{iν}(x) of positive argument
read_scope: Complete 6-page PDF, including appendix and references. Independently reconstructed fixed-argument zero counting through the linear term using I-series and gamma phase; higher expansion coefficients and numerical table not independently recomputed.
main_result: Theorem 1, page 4, equation (3.5): for fixed x>0, ν_n has an asymptotic expansion beginning m/W(2m/(e x)), m=(n+3/4)π, followed by explicit inverse-m corrections. Equation (1.1) supplies the even Fourier integral; equations (2.1)–(2.4) reconstruct the large-order phase.
limitations: Fixed positive argument x; no uniformity in growing x independently established.
Countably many real order zeros cited from earlier source; all-complex-zero exclusion independently reconstructed in audit.
Higher saddle coefficients, subdominant saddles and numerical table read but not deeply audited.
research_questions: Use this classical kernel as a rigorous negative control for Li-prefix and smooth-kernel sufficient conditions.
Track the arithmetic conditions absent from an otherwise RVM-compatible zero count.

title: Asymptotic Estimation for Eigenvalues in the Exponential Potential and for Zeros of K_{iν}(z) with Respect to Order
version: Publisher final, received 15 May 2021, final form 1 June 2021, published 10 June 2021
read_scope: Complete 7-page publisher PDF, all sections, figures, and references. Independently reconstructed the exact spectral/Bessel substitution. Semiclassical full expansion and 10,000-zero numerical dataset were not independently replayed.
main_result: Section 3, pages 3–4, identifies Dirichlet eigenvalues of an exponential half-line Schrödinger potential with imaginary-order K zeros. Equation (7), page 4, gives a Lambert-W asymptotic approximation for the nth positive order zero at fixed z>0. Section 2 derives its classical action and WKB quantization approximation.
limitations: The Bohr–Sommerfeld relation in Section 2 is a semiclassical input, not an exact eigenvalue equation.
Numerical claims and the full claimed remainder in equation (7) have not been independently verified.
This does not identify individual Riemann zeta zeros.
research_questions: Compare exact gamma-phase counting with the WKB action while preserving all normalization factors.
Use the solvable positive kernel to test which spectral/Laplace assumptions fail to enforce an all-zero conclusion.

title: Bemerkung über die Integraldarstellung der Riemannschen ξ-Funktion
version: Original 1926 article; first and last signatures printed March1926; no exact issue date inferred
read_scope: Complete 13-page primary PDF text read; pages306 and315 visually rendered to verify exact integral definition, all-simple-imaginary conclusion and O(1) counting formula. Independent spectral/phase reconstruction of central Bessel result; not every constant in original gamma-series and rectangle argument independently recomputed.
main_result: Equation(7), p306: G(z;a)=∫R exp[−a(e^u+e^(−u))+zu]du, a>0, i.e. 2K_z(2a). Sections1–3 prove every zero simple and purely imaginary. Page315 gives positive-ordinate count y/pi log(y/a)−y/pi+O(1). Therefore K_{w/2}(2π) already has the RVM smooth main through its linear term with O(1) error by the exact substitution z=w/2,a=π. Equation(6), p306 defines the classical symmetrized fake xi function, and pp316–317 prove its real-zero property using HilfssatzII.
proof_architecture: Integration by parts gives difference equation(9), p307.
Gamma expansion(11), pp307–308 yields asymptotic control and initial small-a zero confinement in Section2.
Zero exclusion on Re(z)=±1 follows from the recurrence, conjugation and impossible indefinitely shifted zeros, Section3 IV.
Parameter continuation in a excludes outside-strip zeros, Section3 V.
Argument-principle rectangles and phase control force no nonimaginary zeros and no excess multiplicity, Section3 VI, pp313–315.

HilfssatzI, pp315–316: a first nonzero odd derivative at zero produces an eventual fixed-sign algebraic cosine-transform tail; naive nonsymmetric finite xi-kernel truncations consequently have only finitely many real zeros.
HilfssatzII, pp316–317: symmetric imaginary shifts preserve real zeros for real entire genus0/1 functions with all zeros real and at least one zero; this gives real zeros for the symmetrized fake xi.
limitations: The source does not prove RH or identify individual zeta zeros.
Our quartet perturbation/strict-log-concavity/Li-prefix assembly is not identified in this source; its priority remains unassessed.
The odd-derivative obstruction needs real analyticity at the origin and appropriate derivative decay; do not generalize to arbitrary smooth kernels.
Original formulas were read but the entire original 1926 technical proof is not claimed independently verified.
research_questions: Which arithmetic constraints distinguish the true xi kernel from classical RVM-compatible fake xi kernels?
Use exact symmetric countermodels to test finite certificates while retaining all needed normalization factors.
Trace prior polynomial perturbations and shape constraints before making novelty claims.
